key_insight: PhySGA frames 3D composition as an interactive physics-space agent task, combining planning, simulation, and feedback to assemble objects more reliably than static-prior methods.
engineering_relevance: This is directly relevant to digital content creation and robot simulation because it improves physically plausible assembly for rigid, articulated, and deformable objects.
method: Assembly Agent plans global steps and performs coarse geometric/kinematic adjustments.
Critic Agent diagnoses simulator states using contact dynamics and provides fine-grained closed-loop corrections.
Action Routers execute semantic plans as physical simulator primitives, while a Self-Evolving Skill Library reuses successful trial-and-error experience.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments in Isaac Sim showing improved relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality over existing methods.
watch_item: Performance may depend on simulator fidelity and the quality of agent routing/skills, so transferring the approach to new scenes or simulators could require careful re-tuning.
paper_title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
